sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded at startup in main before the HTTP server starts listening, so /healthz (readiness) cannot pass until the load succeeds.
sonnet.q2: After 3 retries of the whole load (2s apart), it logs the error (secret names only) and exits non-zero; it never becomes ready. The rollout halts and the old pods keep serving, so customers see no errors.
sonnet.q3: A background timer re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes; if a version id changed, the new (value, version_id) pair replaces the old entry in one assignment. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value for any secret it couldn't read, updates the ones it could, logs a warning (name and error, no value), retries next tick, and the app stays running and ready.
sonnet.q4: Held in an in-memory cache in each process, {name: (value, version_id)}. Never written to disk, environment variables or logs.
sonnet.q5: Read: only the orders-api-prod identity (read-only, only on orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call. Engineers have no access to prod.
sonnet.q6: The old values remain in git history, which is not being rewritten, so they count as leaked. Rotating them (new key at provider, then revoking the old key) makes the old values harmless.
sonnet.q7: Clients call secrets.get("<name>") on every outgoing request and put the value in the Authorization header. They no longer copy the key at construction, so the refreshed key is used from the next request with no restart.
sonnet.q8: Check /healthz on every pod (it reports secret version ids, never values) after waiting for the refresh (at most 5 minutes, allow 10). All 4 pods must show the new version id; only then does the security on-call revoke the old key.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access; 2) copy keys into the store; 3) one merge that switches the app to read from the store and removes the keys from the committed file; 4) verify; 5) rotate keys at the providers one at a time; 6) retire pre-migration images. Switching the app and removing keys from the file happen together in step 3.
sonnet.q10: From the secret store at orders-api/dev/* (sandbox keys), under make run with APP_ENV=dev, using the developer's own login.
sonnet.q11: It does not start with a partial set. It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart; if it still fails, it logs the error (names only) and exits non-zero.
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Security has not decided whether or how often keys are rotated on a schedule; the plan covers only the one-time rotation in step 5.
